ledger.claim: The driver's own GPS trace records exactly one continuous hold inside the pickup geofence, running from 17:15:00 to 17:19:00 — 240 seconds, across 25 qualifying fixes, all of them stationary (the only distinct speed in the driver track is 0.0 kph). The minimum dwell for this trip's zone class is 300 seconds: the pickup is Plaza Singapura, a LARGE_VENUE, and 300 seconds is the fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec the policy fixes for that class. That is a 60-second shortfall, and under POL-NS-06 a shortfall means the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full. This is arithmetic, not impression: state the minimum (300), state the measured dwell (240), state the gap (60).

POL-NS-01 is deliberately conjunctive and the driver must carry all four limbs. Limb (c) requires the driver to have held position inside the geofence for a continuous dwell of at least fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec for the zone class, and it fixes the clock at the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not the 'arrived' tap. The longest qualifying run in the trace is 240 seconds against a 300-second minimum for LARGE_VENUE, so limb (c) fails on the driver's own evidence and the fee is not legitimately chargeable under this clause.

The shortfall survives even on the start point most favourable to the driver. The trip record's 'arrived' event is stamped 17:15:20 and the trip was terminated by the driver at 17:19:00 — 220 seconds on that (policy-disfavoured) clock, which is still 80 seconds under the 300-second minimum. POL-NS-01 requires the clock to run from the first in-geofence fix instead, which gives 240 seconds and still fails. On either reading the waiting period the rider is said to have paid for was never served.

There is no traffic advisory on this file to bring POL-NS-06 limb (i) into play. EV-ADVIS-09103-01 carries no payload at all — it is MISSING, weight 0.0 — and the clause requires an advisory that is present and populated with a qualifying type before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed. In any event the trace shows a single in-geofence interval (run_count 1) and 240 seconds of accumulated dwell, so no permissible accumulation could close the 60-second gap, and no traffic advisory may reduce the required minimum in any case.

The driver's statement that 'the rider did not appear' does not answer the claim. POL-NS-06 refunds the fee where the effective dwell falls short 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages' — the waiting period is the consideration the rider paid for. I do not dispute the rider_track: it places the rider's device roughly 519 m from the pin with 0 qualifying rider fixes, and the chat log contains no rider message. None of that changes the outcome under this clause, because the shortfall is a driver-side failure measured entirely from the driver's own fixes.

The amount charged is not itself in dispute and needs no escalation. The SGD 8.00 cancellation-fee line on the fare breakdown reconciles exactly with fee_schedule.resolution_rule: the GREATER of the LARGE_VENUE zone fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00) is SGD 8.00, and the vehicle tier is the dimension that produced it. The rider therefore asks for the cancellation-fee line only — SGD 8.00 — and not for any booking, platform or waiting-time line, which are all zero here.

Nothing in this record engages the escalation machinery, so the dispute can and should be decided on the merits. The trace has no sampling gaps at all (25 fixes at a 10-second cadence, max_gap_sec 0.0), the 'arrived' marker at 17:15:20 sits 20 seconds from the first fix — well inside the 90-second clock-skew threshold — the chat log holds all 3 messages the trip record counts, and the fee reconciles. There is accordingly no POL-NS-08 defect and no POL-NS-09 trigger.

The anti-farming check in POL-NS-07 does not trip, which confirms that no escalation is required before the rider's refund is ordered: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, far below the threshold of 4, and no rate calculation is reached. Nor does any POL-NS-09 limb fire — rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and the counterparty-dispute counters for both parties are 0. The shortfall finding should therefore produce a monetary ruling for the rider, not a hold.

The driver's GPS trace carries 25 consecutive qualifying fixes, every one of them about 24 m from the Plaza Singapura pickup pin, so the POL-NS-02 proximity test is comfortably met — far inside the 120 m arrival radius that applies to a LARGE_VENUE pickup — and the arrival element of POL-NS-01 limb (b) is satisfied.

At the recorded arrival timestamp the driver was stationary — the only speed anywhere in the driver track is 0.0 kph — and roughly 24 m from the pin. Neither POL-NS-05 trigger therefore fires: he was not more than 300 m away, and he was not travelling at 15 kph or above. There is no false-arrival finding available against this driver, and the waiting clock is not to be recomputed.

The trip record shows the trip terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — one of the three codes POL-NS-01 limb (d) expressly recognises — with no boarding event anywhere in the record, so the reason-code element on which limb (d) turns is met on the face of the record.

The SGD 8.00 cancellation fee is exactly the figure the fee_schedule resolution rule produces: the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00). The vehicle-tier dimension produced it, and the fare line reconciles — so there is no integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d) and no basis to attack the amount charged.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not bite on this driver: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, well below the count threshold of 4, and that figure divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d (120) is 0.008, far below the 0.08 rate threshold. Both limbs are required, and neither is met, so driver compensation would not be withheld on these facts.

The rider cannot be exonerated under POL-NS-04. The rider's own track sits about 519 m from the pin with zero qualifying rider fixes inside the 150 m presence radius for this zone class, and the chat log contains no locating or coordinating message from the rider at all — the only driver-directed traffic is the driver's own 'At the mall ride-hail bay' and his cancellation notice. Limbs (a) and (c) both fail, so that clause does not carry the rider's case.

I do not dispute the arithmetic on the waiting period, and I put it to the Judge plainly: the longest qualifying in-geofence run is 240 seconds against the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum, a shortfall of 60 seconds, and because EV-ADVIS-09103-01 is MISSING there is no traffic_advisory that could permit separate in-geofence intervals to be summed under POL-NS-06(i). The driver's genuine arrival, his recognised reason code and a correctly computed fee are on the record; the 60-second dwell shortfall is not something I can argue away, and I do not try to.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you agree on the numbers and the record supports them, so this is decided on the arithmetic.

To the driver: you did arrive and you did wait, but not for long enough. The GPS trace runs from 17:15:00 to 17:19:00 — 25 stationary fixes (0.0 kph) about 24 m from the Plaza Singapura pin, comfortably inside the 120 m arrival radius for a LARGE_VENUE pickup — so the arrival test in POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) are met, and the trip record's RIDER_NO_SHOW code with no boarding event meets limb (d). Limb (c) is where it fails. The continuous hold inside the geofence is 240 seconds (17:15:00 to 17:19:00) against a 300-second minimum for a LARGE_VENUE pickup: a 60-second shortfall. The clock runs from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from your 17:15:20 'arrived' tap, but even on the tap clock (17:15:20 to the 17:19:00 cancellation) the wait is 220 seconds, 80 seconds short. Nothing rescues that: POL-NS-05 does not fire (you were stationary, ~24 m away, not over 300 m out and not at 15 kph), POL-NS-03 does not apply (you were inside the arrival radius, not outside it), and POL-NS-04 does not apply (no locating message from the rider). Under POL-NS-06 a dwell short of the minimum means the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she replied — the waiting period is what the fee buys. The one route to summing separate in-geofence intervals, limb (i), needs a present and populated traffic advisory, and EV-ADVIS-09103-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0), so there is nothing to sum; in any event the trace shows a single interval only.

To the rider: the refund does not depend on where you were. I note the rider track places your device about 519 m from the pin with no qualifying in-radius fixes; that would have defeated POL-NS-04, and it does not matter here, because POL-NS-06 turns on the driver's own fixes.

The amount is not in dispute. The fare breakdown's cancellation-fee line of SGD 8.00 is the GREATER of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00) — the vehicle tier produced it — so there is no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect, and the whole SGD 8.00 is refunded. No driver compensation is payable: POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and POL-NS-06 displaces it here (the anti-farming check would not have tripped in any event — 1 no-show termination in 30 days against 120 completed trips).

Nothing escalates. No POL-NS-08 limb applies (arrival marker 20 seconds from the nearest fix, no trace gaps, all 3 chat messages present, the fee reconciles), and no POL-NS-09 trigger fires (no contradicting artifacts, no counterparty dispute history, no anti-farming trip, no impaired sole evidence). Your statement that you were at the marked bay and the rider did not appear is consistent with the trace, but a rider's absence does not make a short wait chargeable. No clause produces a referral, and no profile field was used as a ground against either party.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
